content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper designs a new deep neural network that takes advantage of components from both convolutional networks and vision Transformer. It identifies the issues in self-attention, and proposes to replace the pairwise correlation with the correlation between regional features and their average. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in both image recognition and a set of downstream tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
As far as I am concerned, this paper has the following strengths:

(1) It provides insights into the potential issues of the self-attention mechanism, which could benefit the design of future deep networks.

(2) The proposed model is able to outperform the previous state-of-the-art on multiple tasks.

(3) In addition to the enhanced accuracy, qualitative results show that the model seems to have better interpretability as well.
 
Nevertheless, there are also important limitations that can not be overlooked:

(1) There is a body of recent studies showing that self-attention may not be a necessary ingredient for achieving good results under the standard setting (e.g., ConvNeXt highlighted in the paper). It is questionable how much value can a model designed under similar philosophy add to the community. While somewhat contradictory, there are also studies arguing that self-attention is beneficial for improving the robustness of models (e.g., [ref1], see below). Does the proposed model help address the robustness issues?

(2) Relating to the previous comment. While the proposed model is advantageous against conventional Transformer models, results in Table 1 show that its improvements over ConvNeXt (a closely related model) are negligible. Moreover, looking at the results in Table 2, it appears that the baseline already outperforms the compared Transformer models, and the improvements brought by the proposed components are merely 0.9%.

(3) Nearly all of the insights about self-attention are drawn from the comparison between the proposed model and conventional Transformer (e.g., ViT and DeiT). It is unclear whether these issues have been addressed in the recent methods. For example, do Transformer models that consider the properties of CNNs (e.g., Swin-T) have better interpretability? To better understand the problem, I believe it is reasonable to further study the interpretability of these methods. Moreover, it would be better to carry out quantitative analysis on interpretability, e.g., estimating the alignment between attention maps and ground truth bounding boxes for image recognition. 

(4) For completeness of the transfer learning experiments, it is also reasonable to compare with models like ConvNeXt and Swin-T, considering that the baseline already outperforms the models compared in Tables 3 and 4. 

[ref1] Are Transformers More Robust Than CNNs? NIPS, 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
(1) The proposed model is well motivated by key issues in self-attention, and the presentation is also easy to understand.

(2) While the model is somewhat novel, it falls into the category of methods that replaces self-attention with more sophisticated designs and learning recipes. Compared to these related studies, its technical contribution is relatively incremental.
content.summary_of_the_review: While this study provides interesting insights into the self-attention mechanism, the advantages of the proposed model are somewhat limited compared to recent methods that follow similar design paradigms. I also have some concerns about the experiments, as the key analyses only take into account the conventional Transformer models. Overall, this is a borderline paper to me. I would consider raising the scores if the authors can provide more complete comparisons/analyses.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a convolutional neural network (ConvNet) upon a hierarchical vision transformer (ViT) based on the observation, where the attention maps by pretrained ViTs including a distilled DeiT are similar regardless of the query points, for given images. The authors further specified the observations two folds: 1) smoothed attentions done by a distillation improve the performance; 2) the query-irrelevant attention does not meet the philosophy the self-attention so can be replaced with a global-context module. The author instantiates the proposed module so-called the FCViT block based on two successive modules consisting of the two convolutional layers: an 11x11  depthwise convolution (dwconv) and a subsequent 1x1 conv. The authors approximate the queries in the self-attention to a one-hot vector based on the observation which is called the global context (GC) and incorporate it as the input of the base convolutional module. The GC module becomes a GAP of the tokens (i.e., projected values) after another approximation. In addition to this, a dynamic approach of GC is proposed by computing the similarity between GAP and the entire tokens with learnable rescaling parameters like a normalization layer. Finally, the multi-group concept looks analogous to the multi-head attention, bottleneck-like module which involves Maxout, and an extra dwconv-involved channel-mixer (i.e., fc-3x3dwconv-fc). The authors show the ImageNet-1k performance comparison with the SOTA network architectures including ViT-based models and some ConvNet/ViT hybrids. The authors demonstrate the models on COCO detection and instance segmentation, and on ADE20k semantic segmentation tasks as well. Some ablation studies are well provided.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros)
+ This paper is well-written.
+ The logical progression based on the observation looks good.
+ I could check the code provided anonymously to understand the mechanism better. However, in other words, it was not easy for me to fully understand the proposed method without reading the code due to some of the missing details. 

Cons)
- Since the authors initiated the claim by visualizing the primitive ViT architectures (ViT-B and DeiT-B), the proposed module should be demonstrated in those architectures, not on the hierarchical ViT.
- Visualizing the sparse attention regardless of the query points for some images looks interesting. Still, I would like to see any statistics that it actually happens in entire point locations and not in particular images.
- The authors did an excellent job of describing the motivation, but some of the design choices which are actually considered for the practitioners do not contain the intuitions. Furthermore, not enough insights into the architectural design are provided to learn.
- The first observation concerning smooth attention is not fully addressed throughout the paper. Furthermore, the distillation from a ConvNet teacher appears to give smooth attention, but the relationship between it and an accuracy improvement has been questionable.
- Some of the notations need to be refined, such as  $S=X\bar{X}$. I could follow the notation after seeing the python code. 
- It seems that computing $S=X\bar{X}$ is very similar to the computation in the self-attention between the tokens and GAP of them, 

Comments)
- I mentioned that computing  $S=X\bar{X}$ performs like another self-attention of the tokens and their GAP. Hence, the authors seem to wipe out self-attention and suddenly involve a similar one for the performance. 
- The authors do not seem to revisit the first observation related to smooth attention in the paper. 
- The competitive information bottleneck (CIB) module does not seem to follow the information bottleneck concept; it is rather a bottleneck-like module with the Maxout operation for the intermediate features. It would be better for the authors to clarify this if the module is indeed based on the information bottleneck.
- Towards Eq. (6), I think approximating the softmax to the GAP is not that simple because there is a learnable projection in the keys. Can the authors give any rationale behind it or some experimental results to justify the approximation? 
- I think the authors can measure the throughputs in CoatNet, CvT, Conformer, and so on using the publicly released architecture. Please report the throughput in Table 1.
- There are some recently proposed ConvNets: Patch-ConvNets and Large-kernel ConvNets. Since most of them are still in progress works, it would be interesting to see if the proposed method can beat them:
  -  Augmenting Convolutional networks with attention-based aggregation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.13692)
  -  Patches Are All You Need (https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09792)
  -  31x31 Scaling Up Your Kernels to 31x31: Revisiting Large Kernel Design in CNNs, CVPR 2022
- ConvNext and other ConvNets should be compared in Table 3 and Table 4.
- Some intuitions or insights behind the architectural design choices are missing, for example: 
  - About incorporating $S=X\bar{X}$ over using GAP
  - Why do the authors sum the GCs from the input of equation (4)? 
  - Is the Maxout of two features in the CIB module necessary? 
  - Why should the token mixer module be used successively? Why does it work better?
  - The authors design the base building block with the depthwise convolution (dwconv), which has been known as an inefficient option, so any intuitions about choosing it instead of using the regular convolution.
- Minors
  - Tables on p.15 should be rearranged. 
  - In Fig.5, the upper module should be the channel-attention module.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The proposed module looks novel, but some of the details which do not fall into the contributions of this paper, seem to contribute more to the performance. For example, using more extra convolutions in the module (e.g., dwconv in FFN) improves the performance more, which has been known to the practitioners and also mentioned by the authors, so the comparison with other methods including ConvNets may not be fair.

- The authors provide the training code with the proposed module inside, and it seems to me that training with the given code would reproduce the reported numbers.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper starts with interesting observations, and the formulation of the proposed module looks sound. The performance evaluation is well done compared with the recent backbones. However, due to the comments above, I am currently leaning toward rejecting this work. After seeing the other reviewers' comments and my concerns are well addressed by the authors' responses, the final score can be raised.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper investigates two phenomenons in vision transformers, i.e., the attention maps are almost query-irrelevant in deep layers; the attention maps are sparse. Based on these observations, a fully convolutional vision transformer that inspired by MetaFormer is proposed. Experiments are conducted on standard ImageNet, MS COCO, and ADE20K datasets, showing more competitive performance than other variants.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1. The paper is generally in a good shape and easy to follow.

2. The results are competitive in image classification, while the semantic segmentation result is a bit weak.  

3. The observation of identical attention maps in deep layers is interesting.

Weakness:

1. The concept of the token mixer and channel mixer is introduced by MetaFormer and has not been widely used in the transformer community yet. Putting it in the title may raise some questions for general readers. I would suggest changing it to more reader-friendly expressions.

2. The structure of the proposed network is based on MetaFormer while replacing the token mixer with convolutional layers. Since it involves global context in token mixing, it can achieve a global field of view in theory. However, it is not the first pure convolution solution that can achieve the global field of view.  For example, the Non-local Neural Networks (CVPR18) is the first work that introduces the attention mechanism to convolutional networks. It would be nice to see the comparison between these two methods and the results' justifications.

3. What is the memory consumption of the proposed model?

4. Figure 1 is not clear. It takes me a while to figure out the meaning of each column, i.e., the query point and its corresponding attention map. I think it means the 1xn attention map and reshaping it back to the image size for better visualization.

5. The observation of sparse attention maps is not new. It is actually the main motivation for the sparse transformer. This paper indicates that by smoothing the attention map, the performance can be improved. It is an interesting claim. However, other than some empirical results,  there are no assumptions or theoretical support for this claim. It is interesting that in NLP tasks, this claim does not hold. But for CV tasks, it seems to be valid. 

6. More recent linear transformer based/softmax-free transformers should also be included in the experiment. For example, the SOFT (NeurIPS21), and the Vicinity Vision Transformer.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is in a good shape and the source code is provided for reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The novelty of the method is limited and some of the claims need more support or explanation.

The results on downstream tasks are a bit weak. Experiments on larger models may be needed as I observed that some models may have different behavior in small and large models, i.e., the performance of the smaller one is better than others while the larger one may not.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.

content.title: Connection to global convolutional layers
content.comment:
Dear authors,

Thank you very much for your contribution! 

I was wondering whether you have any insights on the relation of self-attention and global CNNs. Recently, multiple approaches have emerged which propose using global convolutional kernels, e.g., CKConv [1], S4 [2]. In your analysis, you always consider the case in which convolutional layers use small kernels, e.g., 3x3, 7x7. I was wondering whether you have any insights regarding how your analysis would extrapolate to conv kernels of global size. I am personally inclined to think that global conv kernels are already good enough and that the power of self-attention comes mainly from its ability to gather global context.

I would love to hear your opinion on the matter :)

Cheers,

David


**References**

[1] Romero, David W., et al. "Ckconv: Continuous kernel convolution for sequential data." arXiv preprint arXiv:2102.02611 (2021).

[2] Gu, Albert, Karan Goel, and Christopher Ré. "Efficiently modeling long sequences with structured state spaces." arXiv preprint arXiv:2111.00396 (2021).

content.title: Open Disucssions
content.comment:
Hi David, 

Thanks for your open discussions and your interest. 

Here are our responses, which are not part of the rebuttal. Since we are unfamiliar with NLP, our insights will be limited to CV.

------

**1. About our experiments (which convolutional layers use small kernels, e.g., 3x3, 7x7).**

The reason behind our design is that global context is already introduced in our model, and increasing the kernel size (e.g., to 31, 51, etc.) in convolution would not bring further improvements (supported by analysis in Sec. Kernel Size). We did not try bigger sizes or even global conv. We assume this can be done based on ConvNeXt since no global context is introduced in ConvNeXt, and the performance variances can be attributed to kernel size change.r

------

**2. Insights on the relation of self-attention and global CNNs.**

First, we have never tried global CNNs, and thanks for the interesting references; we will have a read. Second, we notice that a larger kernel size will always achieve better performance for pure (depth-wise) ConvNets, referring RepLKNet [1], SLaK [2], and oral reports from the authors of ConvNeXt [3]. However, a simple global conv is never explored. 

[1] Ding, Xiaohan, et al. "Scaling up your kernels to 31x31: Revisiting large kernel design in cnns." CVPR. 2022.

[2] Liu, Shiwei, et al. "More convnets in the 2020s: Scaling up kernels beyond 51x51 using sparsity." arXiv. 2022.

[3] Liu, Zhuang, et al. "A convnet for the 2020s." CVPR. 2022.

------

**3. Personal insights on conv and attention.**

Thank you for sharing your personal insights, and we agree with you. After discussing with many researchers from both industry and academia, we believe that convolution can effortlessly achieve comparable or even better performance than attention variants (also pointed out by Reviewer dAMX). However, ViT will generalize better when scaling the model size and data size to a very large scale (like billion parameters and billion images). 

------

Thanks for your post, discussion, and interest in our work. 

Feel free to discuss more under this thread.

Best,

Authors
